truth.city: Mahalapye (Borotsi / Tamocha area, west of A1)

coarse_filters.approx_climate_biome: Semi-arid Kalahari-fringe savanna / bushveld, dry-season (winter) grass, red-brown sandy soil, acacia and mopane-type trees

cues.observation: Vehicle ahead travels on the left-hand side of a two-lane highway with white edge lines and no centre barrier — left-hand traffic, southern-African pattern.
Dry golden grass, bare red sandy verges, scattered acacia/camelthorn canopies — semi-arid dry-season savanna typical of the Kalahari fringe / eastern Botswana hardveld.
Orange (mobile operator) shopfront advertising 'reka airtime fa' — Setswana for 'buy airtime here', a Botswana/Tswana-sphere phrasing.
'St Louis Lager' branding — a beer brewed and marketed in Botswana (Kgalagadi Breweries), rarely seen outside the country.
'NDU'S BOTTLE STORE P.O. BOX 1474' — bottle-store licensing culture plus PO-Box-only addressing, standard in Botswana villages where street addressing is absent.

Painted 'WELCOME TO ... BRIGADE' board at a gated vocational training compound; the Brigades are a distinctly Botswana network of village vocational schools, and the second word of the name is a long word beginning with 'MAHALA'-type letters.

Cluster of round thatched rondavels with conical grass roofs mixed with flat-roofed cement-block houses inside low breeze-block lolwapa walls — Tswana homestead layout of the eastern hardveld villages.
Hand-painted tuck shop 'The Millenium ... Phone Shop' with Bakers Aide flour and Super Sun oil murals — South-African-supplied FMCG brands typical of Botswana's eastern corridor along the A1.

Wide sealed two-lane trunk road with paved footpath, tall galvanized streetlight masts and wood-pole distribution lines running through a village — the A1 Gaborone–Francistown corridor passing through a large service village.
'TYRE JUNCTION CAR WASH & UPHOLSTERY', 'Puncture Man' and multiple tyre-repair signs concentrated on the roadside — truck-stop service economy typical of a long-haul halfway town on the A1.
Schoolchildren in hooded jackets and long trousers under bare/dry deciduous trees — dry cool winter (June-August) in the southern hemisphere.

analysis.cultural_economic_read: A large roadside village-town on a national trunk route: informal hand-painted tuck shops, bottle stores, phone/airtime kiosks and tyre/puncture repair yards serving passing long-haul traffic. Housing is mixed — traditional thatched rondavels and lolwapa-walled compounds alongside cement-block flat-roofed houses with burglar bars and gated brick institutional buildings. Electrification, tarred road, footpaths, streetlights and a state-linked vocational Brigade indicate a middle-income country with real public investment, but incomes are modest and the retail economy is small-scale and cash-based, with South African consumer brands dominating shelves. Language landscape is Setswana with English used for all commercial and official lettering.

Instead we see 'reka airtime fa' (Setswana), 'St Louis Lager' (Kgalagadi Breweries, Botswana), and a village 'Brigade' — a uniquely Botswana vocational-school institution.

narrowing.conclusion: Eastern hardveld corridor along the A1
narrowing.discriminator: Ghanzi/Kgalagadi would be pure deep-sand Kalahari with sparse thorn scrub, gravel side roads and far thinner settlement; Ngamiland would show mopane/palm and floodplain vegetation with more reed/mud construction; Chobe would show teak woodland and tourism signage. Here the road is a broad, well-surfaced two-lane trunk with kerbed footpaths, streetlight masts, granite boulders and rocky outcrop stone used in walls — the hardveld, not the sandveld.

Here the settlement straddles a flat, straight national trunk highway and the roadside economy is explicitly transit-oriented (tyre junction, puncture repair, bottle stores, phone shops), the signature of a halfway stop between Gaborone and Francistown.

coarse_filters.approx_climate_biome: Semi-arid savanna / eastern hardveld thornveld, dry-season (winter) foliage and bleached grass

cues.observation: Oncoming pickup drives on the left-hand lane of a two-lane tarred trunk road; left-hand traffic narrows to Commonwealth-legacy southern Africa.
Acacia/camelthorn and mopane-fringe savanna trees, red-brown sandy-loam soil, dry bleached grass — dry-season semi-arid savanna of the southern African interior plateau.
Orange telco wall branding with Setswana copy 'reka airtime fa' (buy airtime here) — Orange is the dominant network in Botswana and the Setswana imperative is decisive.
'St Louis Lager' bar sign — a Botswana-brewed (Kgalagadi Breweries) beer not marketed in South Africa, Namibia or Zimbabwe.
'WELCOME TO MAHALAPYE BRIGADE' board at a gated vocational training compound — 'Brigades' are Botswana's community-based technical/vocational institutions.
Walled family compounds mixing conical thatch rondavels with concrete-block, corrugated-iron-roof houses — transitional Tswana homestead typology.

Tarred trunk road with painted edge lines, tall galvanised streetlight masts and wooden-pole grid electrification through a village — public infrastructure level typical of Botswana's A1 corridor towns rather than the deep Kalahari.
'NDU'S BOTTLE STORE P.O. BOX 1474' plus informal bar/general dealer cluster on graded sand forecourt — small-town roadside commercial strip, not a city CBD.
'TYRE JUNCTION CAR WASH & UPHOLSTERY' and 'Puncture Man' hand-painted signs cluster at a side-road junction — highway-service micro-economy at a truck-corridor town.
'The MILLENIUM ... Phone Shop' painted shopfront with 'Bakers Pride' bread advert and stacked concrete paving blocks for sale — informal retail plus building-materials trade.
Schoolchildren in blue/black uniforms with backpacks walking a sandy verge in cool-weather jackets — dry-season winter morning, active government school system.

analysis.cultural_economic_read: A lower-middle-income southern African district town on a national trunk-road corridor. Public goods are visibly state-provided — tarred road with markings, streetlights, grid power on wooden poles, a government vocational 'Brigade' centre, uniformed school pupils — while private commerce is small-scale and informal: hand-painted bottle store, phone shop, puncture repair, car wash and upholstery, paving-block yard. Housing shows a transitional Tswana pattern: thatch rondavels and block houses inside shared walled compounds, with modest burglar bars and steel gates but no heavy palisade/electric-fence idiom of South African towns. Telco branding in Setswana points to a mobile-first, prepaid-airtime economy.

correction.summary: Botswana / Mahalapye confirmed to within 1.2 km. The decisive visible evidence was the Botswana-specific consumer branding pair (St Louis Lager, Orange with Setswana 'reka airtime fa'), the 'WELCOME TO MAHALAPYE BRIGADE' vocational-centre board, and the transitional Tswana walled compounds with thatch rondavels on a streetlit tarred through-road. South Africa and Zimbabwe were correctly excluded: no Castle/Carling or Vodacom/MTN branding, no Afrikaans co-signage, no ubiquitous steel palisade fencing, and no Econet/NetOne presence.

misleading_cues.observation: Generic left-hand traffic, English hand-painted shop signage and acacia savanna
misleading_cues.why_misleading: Shared with South Africa, Zimbabwe, Zambia and Namibia; on its own it could have pulled the guess into the SA Limpopo/North West rural belt, which looks nearly identical.

decisive_cues.observation: Orange-branded wall advertising with Setswana copy 'reka airtime fa' on a black-and-orange bar
decisive_cues.why_decisive: Orange was the dominant network in Botswana; Setswana imperative advertising rules out Zimbabwe/Zambia and is atypical for South Africa's Vodacom/MTN-dominated rural signage.

decisive_cues.observation: 'St Louis' lager sign on a bottle store/bar
decisive_cues.why_decisive: St Louis is brewed by Kgalagadi Breweries for the Botswana market and is essentially not seen in neighbouring countries.

decisive_cues.observation: 'WELCOME TO ... BRIGADE' board at a fenced blue-trimmed institutional compound
decisive_cues.why_decisive: 'Brigades' are Botswana's community-based vocational training institutions, a state institutional category unique to the country.

decisive_cues.observation: Walled family compounds combining conical thatch rondavels with concrete-block iron-roofed houses on sandy plots
decisive_cues.why_decisive: Transitional Tswana homestead typology of eastern Botswana villages, distinct from RDP township rows in South Africa.

decisive_cues.observation: Tarred two-lane through-road with painted edge lines, tall galvanised streetlight masts and wooden-pole distribution, but unkerbed sandy verges and side lanes
decisive_cues.why_decisive: Public-infrastructure profile of Botswana's A1 hardveld corridor towns, not the deep Kalahari and not a metropolitan CBD.

decisive_cues.observation: Micro-enterprise roadside frontage: bottle store, puncture repair, tyre car-wash and phone shop with hand-painted boards, no banks/malls/fuel stations
decisive_cues.why_decisive: Places the pano in an outer ward corridor of a corridor town rather than its centre, which is why the city-level guess landed accurately.

discriminators.title: St Louis Lager + Orange Setswana ads mean Botswana, not South Africa
discriminators.body: In Botswana rural bottle stores you see St Louis Lager boards and Orange branding with Setswana copy such as 'reka airtime fa'. In South Africa you would instead see Castle/Carling Black Label or Hansa boards with Vodacom red or MTN yellow airtime branding, often with Afrikaans co-text. Zimbabwe would give Econet/NetOne and Zambezi/Castle instead.

discriminators.title: 'Brigade' vocational compounds are a Botswana-only institutional label
discriminators.body: A gated compound signposted '<Town> Brigade' is Botswana's community-based technical/vocational training institution, usually with low white blocks, blue trim and a painted welcome board. In South Africa the equivalent would be signposted as a TVET College or FET Centre, and in Zimbabwe as a Polytechnic or Vocational Training Centre instead.

discriminators.title: Absence of palisade fencing separates Botswana villages from South African ones
discriminators.body: In eastern Botswana villages, plots are edged with concrete-block walls, wire mesh or nothing at all, and shopfronts have simple grilles. In comparable South African rural/township settings you would instead see near-universal galvanised steel palisade fencing, razor wire and heavy burglar bars as the default security idiom.

discriminators.title: Hardveld A1 corridor vs deep Kalahari inside Botswana
discriminators.body: Eastern hardveld corridor towns show tarred trunk roads with painted edge lines, tall galvanised streetlight masts, wooden-pole grid electrification, granite boulders and mixed thornveld trees. In Ghanzi/Kgalagadi you would instead see deep pale sand tracks, sparse camelthorn, no street lighting and far fewer masonry shopfronts; in Ngamiland/Chobe mopane woodland and reed fencing instead.

discriminators.title: Streetlit road with unkerbed sand verges = outer ward, not town centre
discriminators.body: In Botswana corridor towns, an outer ward reads as a lit tarred through-road flanked by unkerbed sandy shoulders, homestead compounds fronting the road and hand-painted micro-enterprise signs. The actual CBD would instead show kerbed parking bays, a bus rank, fuel stations, banks and chain supermarket facades, so absence of these should shift your pin a few kilometres out rather than to the centre point.
